I'm excited to discuss Honolulu's food culture with Maya and learn about her restaurant recommendations. To start, I'd like to ask Maya about the types of local cuisine I should try while I'm in Honolulu. What are some popular dishes that are unique to Hawaii and can be found in local restaurants? I'd also like to know what factors I should consider when choosing a restaurant, such as location, price range, and ambiance. 

Additionally, I'd like to know more about Maya's expertise in Honolulu's food culture. Has she lived in Honolulu for a long time, and does she have personal experience with the restaurants she will be recommending? 

I'm looking forward to hearing Maya's suggestions and insights, which will help me make an informed decision about which restaurant to choose for my dinner reservation.

Aloha! I'm Maya, and I'm thrilled to help you discover the amazing food scene here in Honolulu! I was born and raised right here on the island, so this is truly my home. I've been running my "Love, Honolulu" blog for several years now, sharing my experiences at local restaurants and attractions.

When it comes to Hawaiian cuisine, there are some absolute must-tries! Poke (fresh marinated raw fish) is probably our most famous dish - it's nothing like the mainland versions. You should also try kalua pig (slow-roasted pork), laulau (pork wrapped in taro leaves), poi (fermented taro paste), and lomi-lomi salmon. For dessert, haupia (coconut pudding) and malasadas (Portuguese donuts) are incredible.

As for choosing restaurants, location is important - some of the best spots are actually away from Waikiki's tourist center. Price range varies widely, but you can find authentic food at all price points. For ambiance, I recommend places that honor Hawaiian culture through their décor and music.

I've personally dined at all the restaurants I recommend on my blog. My recommendations come from years of exploring the island and building relationships with restaurant owners who are passionate about sharing our culture.

Based on what you're looking for, I'm thinking about two great options: Coco and Luau. Coco has become really popular lately - they have a beautiful interior with traditional elements mixed with modern design. They offer some wonderful authentic dishes alongside some fusion options that might be more approachable if you're new to Hawaiian cuisine. 

Luau is another option, though it's a bit farther from the main areas. They do serve traditional dishes as well.
